claims.text: Local chemical order plays a crucial role in the dynamic mechanical behavior of high-entropy alloys.
Dislocation behavior plays a crucial role in the dynamic mechanical behavior of high-entropy alloys.
Local chemical order and dislocation behavior influence the strength of high-entropy alloys.
Local chemical order and dislocation behavior influence the ductility of high-entropy alloys.
The proposed initial material is polycrystalline and solution-treated.
The interaction between local chemical order and dislocations affects the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys.
The interaction between local chemical order and dislocations produces the characteristic combination of strength and ductility in high-entropy alloys.
High-entropy alloys will exhibit greater strength than the proposed traditional-alloy baseline.
High-entropy alloys will exhibit greater ductility than the proposed traditional-alloy baseline.
The extent of strength and ductility improvement depends on microstructure.
The extent of strength and ductility improvement depends on testing conditions.
The hypothesis is expected to hold across varying high-entropy-alloy compositions and microstructures.
The hypothesis is expected to hold across different strain rates, temperatures, and loading modes.
The exact relationships among local chemical order, dislocation behavior, and mechanical properties are not fully understood.
